audit_findings.title: Unmodeled separation-tax indemnity could rank ahead of common equity
audit_findings.mechanism: Any indemnification obligation would be deducted in the equity bridge ahead of common equity and is absent from the current bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: In the event that LGL Group suffers tax-related losses in connection with the Separation that must be indemnified by us under the Tax Agreement, the indemnification liability could have a material adverse effect on us.
audit_findings.explanation: The contractual indemnity is demonstrated, but a payable loss is not: the latest 10-Q reports no Distribution-related tax recorded and no legal contingency accrual. The agreement's exposure, covenant compliance and any tax examination remain unknown, so the record cannot establish materiality or safely treat the liability as zero.
audit_findings.action: Review the Tax Agreement, tax opinions, covenant-compliance certifications, examination correspondence and indemnification notices; obtain a probability-weighted or maximum exposure and rerun the equity bridge if supported.

audit_findings.title: The 2025 owner-earnings anchor may omit recurring incentive compensation
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.5 million, equal to 23.1% of the $6.5 million anchor; the first-half 2026 filing identifies $1.452 million of stock compensation related to 2025 bonuses
audit_findings.mechanism: An omitted recurring incentive burden inflates anchor owner earnings and every forecast year; equity-settled compensation may instead enter through dilution, requiring reconciliation to fully diluted shares.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company's total costs and expenses for 2024 included bonus expense of approximately $1.5 million, or 3.0% of revenues, which was not incurred in 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate that 2025 had no recorded bonus expense while $470 thousand of manufacturing cost and $982 thousand of engineering, selling and administrative expense recognized in 2026 related to 2025 bonuses. That timing item is large enough to change the valuation conclusion. It remains unresolved whether the $4.649665 million fully diluted share count captures the complete economic burden, so simply deducting the expense could double count dilution.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the 2025 bonus obligation, 2026 awards, vesting and issued or reserved shares to the fully diluted share count; determine the recurring cash-versus-equity mix and rerun the valuation using one consistent treatment.

audit_findings.title: Customer concentration creates downside not represented by a zero-growth bear case
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 combined revenue exposure of $27.715 million, or 50.9% of revenue; first-half 2026 exposure of $16.871 million, or 56.6%
audit_findings.mechanism: Loss or repricing of a concentrated customer would reduce the starting owner-earnings level and potentially margins and working-capital recovery, rather than merely reduce the growth rate to zero.
audit_findings.evidence: For the year ended December 31, 2025, our largest and second largest customers accounted for 36.0% and 14.9% of the Company's total revenues, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The concentration is demonstrated, but no customer loss or repricing is presently shown; first-half 2026 sales to the two customers increased in concentration, and backlog reached $83.968 million. This is therefore a forward-looking downside that the flat-earnings bear case does not capture, not a demonstrated current earnings error.
audit_findings.action: Obtain customer-specific margins, contract duration, termination and repricing rights, program funding and backlog composition; rerun a permanent earnings step-down for loss or repricing of each major customer.

audit_findings.title: Transitional related-party arrangements may understate standalone recurring costs
audit_findings.magnitude: Current TSA income was $48 thousand in 2025 and $24 thousand in first-half 2026; LGL employee-cost reimbursements were $41 thousand in 2025 and $56 thousand in first-half 2026; replacement cost is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Termination of shared services could increase recurring operating expenses and reduce sustainable owner earnings; unresolved separation claims could instead require an equity-bridge deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: The LGL Group, Inc. continues to perform functions for us, and we continue to perform functions for The LGL Group, Inc., on a transitional basis, and as a result, we may experience operational disruptions and incur significant costs to perform these functions ourselves following the transition period or be subject to claims and liability.
audit_findings.explanation: The current recorded related-party flows are small relative to the $6.5 million anchor, but that comparison does not measure the cost of replacing LGL-provided functions. Because the TSA remained active through June 2026 and no quantified transition plan or current disruption is supplied, the possible incremental cost is forward-looking rather than a demonstrated omission.
audit_findings.action: Inventory all shared services, contractual termination dates, allocated personnel and systems; obtain a standalone replacement-cost budget and rerun owner earnings if the incremental annual cost is significant.
